title: Demo failure modes + backup plan (working doc)
content:
Context
- Goal: no demo should fail “on stage” due to predictable issues (quota, auth, model churn, empty dashboards). If something breaks, we switch smoothly to a backup path that still tells the story.
- Audience: AE/SE running 20–45 min demos; also useful for PMM when building backup screenshots/recording.
- This doc is intentionally scrappy. We’ll turn the stable parts into a short “Backup Mode” card + Confluence runbook links.

Definitions / quick principles
- “Happy path” = live demo app + console tour on the demo tenant.
- “Backup mode” = continue the narrative with screenshots / recording / canned outputs while we fix live issues in parallel.
- Rule #1: never blame the product or the prospect’s network. Treat breakage as “let’s switch to an offline view while we keep moving.”
- Rule #2: preserve the storyline (economics + reliability + observability). The backup should still prove the point.

Standard pre-flight (10 minutes before call)
- Run demo tenant healthcheck (see ENG-4862 / PR-28531).
- Confirm you have the correct scoped key + project selected (avoid last-minute RBAC surprises).
- Open Console tabs ahead of time: Overview dashboard, Cost breakdown, Latency, Errors, Routes/Rollouts.
- Trigger synthetic traffic generator if graphs look thin (PR-28488 / ENG-4833).
- Keep the backup assets ready: local folder or Drive links (recording + screenshots + canned JSON outputs).

Backup asset inventory (what we should always have ready)
- 5–7 min recording: “Core API + streaming + tool calling + structured output” (ideal: with voiceover).
- 3–5 annotated screenshots: Console (cost/token breakdown, latency, errors, rollout/canary view, audit log snippet).
- Canned outputs:
  - Example streaming transcript (copy/paste) for the chat completion.
  - Example structured output JSON showing schema compliance.
  - Example tool call payload + tool result + final answer.
  - Example fallback event: request fails primary route → served by fallback model/region with header/metadata.
- “If Console is down” PDF: short slide-like view with the 4 graphs we need + explanation (ask Design to package from DES-611 screenshots).

Failure modes + detection + fixes + backup paths

1) Quota / rate limiting (429) during live demo
- Symptoms
  - Requests error with 429 / “throttled”
  - Streaming starts then stops; retry also fails
  - Demo app feels “laggy” under parallel demos
- Most likely causes
  - Too many parallel demos on same project/key
  - Synthetic traffic job + live demo competing
  - Default rate limits too low for the scripted burst
- Fast detection
  - Healthcheck shows quota pressure or recent 429 spike
  - Console Errors chart spikes (if it’s working)
- Immediate actions (in-call)
  - Reduce concurrency in demo app scenario runner; switch to single request steps
  - Move to backup mode for the “core API” segment (recording + canned outputs)
  - Keep the story moving: “We’ll show you what the output looks like and the operational view; we can run it live again at the end.”
- Fix (after / parallel)
  - Follow demo-capacity-and-quotas runbook; request temp quota bump or switch to isolated project
  - Check SUP-4127 learnings; adjust automation defaults
- Backup plan
  - Use recording for API calls; use screenshots for Console graphs
  - Use canned outputs to demonstrate tool calling/structured JSON
  - Optional: switch to a second “spare” project (needs to exist + be seeded)

2) Auth / RBAC misconfiguration (can’t access org/project; key invalid)
- Symptoms
  - SE can’t log in / missing permissions
  - API key returns 401/403
  - Console shows “no access” or blank project selector
- Likely causes
  - New SE not added to demo org group; SSO mapping drift
  - Key rotation happened, doc wasn’t updated
  - Using the wrong tenant (non-demo) or wrong environment
- Fast detection
  - Healthcheck: auth/rbac section fails
  - Console login works but project list empty
- Immediate actions (in-call)
  - Don’t troubleshoot SSO live. Switch to backup mode immediately.
  - Use recording + screenshots for the full console tour.
  - If the prospect cares about SSO: narrate with the “enterprise/security screenshots” (SAML/RBAC/audit logs).
- Fix
  - Escalate via internal helpdesk pattern (see INT-993); verify group mapping + role
  - Re-issue scoped key (ENG-4855 / PR-28577)
- Backup plan
  - Recording + static console screenshots
  - If needed, do the rest of the meeting as a discovery + architecture review (still valuable)

3) Console dashboards empty / stale (no metrics)
- Symptoms
  - Graphs are blank; no cost/latency/errors; “No data in selected time range”
  - Traces view shows nothing
- Likely causes
  - Synthetic traffic job not running or ingestion lag
  - Wrong time range / wrong project selected
  - Ingestion pipeline hiccup
  - Known UX empty-state bug resurfaced (ref PR-28644)
- Fast detection
  - Healthcheck flags dashboard freshness
  - Errors/usage not visible after you run a test request
- Immediate actions (in-call)
  - First try: switch time range to “Last 15 minutes” and confirm project
  - Run a single request from demo app and refresh once
  - If still empty after 60–90 seconds: switch to screenshots of the exact same views
  - Narration: “We seed synthetic traffic to keep these views representative; here’s what the breakdown typically looks like.”
- Fix
  - Trigger synthetic traffic generator (PR-28488)
  - Confirm ingestion status / alerts (ENG-4879)
- Backup plan
  - Screenshot pack with callouts for the 4 required console proof points
  - Keep a short “token-level breakdown” screenshot + explain the levers (batching/caching)

4) Model/version churn breaks expected outputs (demo regression)
- Symptoms
  - Structured output fails schema / tool calls differ from script
  - Latency/cost numbers drift dramatically from our narrative
  - A/B rollout view doesn’t match the “known-good” story
- Likely causes
  - Route not pinned to the demo version
  - Fallback policy changed
  - Model catalog update or backend deploy changed defaults
- Fast detection
  - The first scripted scenario doesn’t match expected output
  - Healthcheck warns about model pin mismatch
- Immediate actions (in-call)
  - Avoid arguing over exact output. Pivot to “the mechanism” (how routing/rollouts work) and show a canned output that matches what we intended.
  - If reliability segment depends on fallback behavior: use the pre-captured fallback screenshot + headers.
- Fix
  - Verify model pin config + fallback policy (ADR + ENG-4840)
  - Re-run the “known-good” scenario suite and update expected outputs only if approved
- Backup plan
  - Canned JSON outputs for structured output + tool calling
  - Recording made against the pinned build

5) Capacity constraints / “noisy neighbor” perception during Dedicated narrative
- Symptoms
  - Latency spikes unpredictably mid-demo
  - Prospect asks “is this shared?” and the performance looks inconsistent
- Likely causes
  - Demo tenant running on shared hosted pool or burst is constrained
  - Parallel demos using same resources
- Immediate actions (in-call)
  - Use this as a segue: explain Hosted vs Dedicated and why Dedicated exists
  - Switch the live portion to simpler requests (smaller prompts) OR move to recording
  - Show the “Dedicated controls” screenshot / slide (capacity isolation, autoscaling policy)
- Fix
  - Follow demo-capacity-and-quotas runbook; isolate projects; schedule heavy demos
- Backup plan
  - “Dedicated story” is mostly narrative + architecture diagrams; ensure those are in the deck appendix

6) Streaming disconnects / flakey network / browser issues
- Symptoms
  - Streaming stops halfway; client reconnect fails; SSE/websocket errors
- Likely causes
  - Local network / corporate VPN / region-specific issue (see SUP-4302)
  - Browser extension interference
- Immediate actions (in-call)
  - Don’t debug networking. Play the streaming recording.
  - Paste the streamed transcript as text while narrating.
- Fix
  - Try alternate region endpoint; alternate client (curl) for SE only (not “on stage”)
- Backup plan
  - Recording + transcript

7) Demo reset / seed data not ready (routes missing, keys expired, wrong project)
- Symptoms
  - Demo app errors due to missing route/model
  - Console lacks seeded prompt sets/evals
- Likely causes
  - Reset job partially failed
  - SE using a non-standard project
- Immediate actions (in-call)
  - If core API still works, focus on API + narrative and use screenshots for ops
  - Otherwise, full backup mode
- Fix
  - Run demo-tenant-reset runbook; rotate keys as needed; verify “known-good” checklist
- Backup plan
  - Always have a “spare” project that is kept warm (seeded + traffic) — TODO: decide if this is required for v1

Backup mode scripts (suggested phrasing)
- When switching to backup mode:
  - “To keep us on time, I’m going to switch to an offline view of the same flow. You’ll still see the exact requests, outputs, and the operational screens; we can rerun it live at the end or in a follow-up.”
- If asked “is something down?”
  - “The demo environment is isolated and intentionally throttled for safety. Rather than troubleshoot live, we’ll use our recorded run and focus on what matters: latency/cost controls and the reliability story.”
- If Console is empty:
  - “This view depends on telemetry ingestion; we keep a synthetic workload running so the graphs represent a realistic distribution. Here’s the exact breakdown you’d see in a production tenant.”

Who to ping / escalation (during a live incident)
- Primary: #demo-oncall (or current alias) + tag Sean Gallagher for SRE escalation when availability/quotas are impacted.
- Console data issues: tag Logan Wright / Mei Lin.
- Auth/RBAC issues: tag Ethan Park.
- Model pinning / fallback: tag Mina Haddad / Ravi Menon.
- Note: for the live call, one person stays “customer-facing” while a second person pings internally.

TODOs / open questions
- Do we require a second spare project per region for parallel demos? (relates to ENG-4894)
- Do we want a pre-generated “exec 15-min” recording vs full 30-min? (Marketing asked in Slack)
- Consolidate backup assets into one Drive folder with a stable link (and an offline version for travel).
- Decide the minimum screenshots needed for v1 certification (Elliot to propose).

Notes from the field (keep updating)
- 2025-11: 429s during live demo when synthetic traffic job overlapped with scenario runner (see SUP-4127).
- 2025-11: empty dashboards panic → workaround was to run synthetic traffic job and adjust time range (see Slack sales thread 1741446203).
- 2025-12: new SE lacked RBAC mapping after SSO group change (see INT-993).

Appendix: “Minimum viable proof” if everything is broken
- Show:
  1) One API request + output (recording)
  2) One cost breakdown screenshot
  3) One latency chart screenshot
  4) One reliability/fallback screenshot + explanation
  5) One security screenshot (audit log snippet + SSO/RBAC mention)
- Then end with next steps: offer a POC plan + follow-up technical deep dive.
